proposed.text: According to Trap #40?, what are the two values that examinees frequently swap when describing the tactile warning strip specification — and which value is the depth versus the setback?

options.text: Depth = 300 mm; setback = 600 mm from the hazard edge — the strip is narrow and placed well back
Depth = 600 mm; setback = 300 mm from the hazard edge — the strip is wide and placed close to the hazard
Depth = 600 mm; setback = 600 mm from the hazard edge — both dimensions are equal for simplicity
Depth = 300 mm; setback = 300 mm from the hazard edge — both dimensions match for easy recall

rationale.summary: Trap #40: depth = 600 mm (the strip itself); setback = 300 mm (how far back from the hazard it is placed).
rationale.explanation: Trap #40 in the article describes this as the most-swapped pair of numbers in tactile specification. The tactile warning strip is 600 mm deep — meaning the strip occupies 600 mm of floor space measured perpendicular to the hazard. The near edge of the strip is placed 300 mm back from the hazard edge (stair nosing, ramp top, platform edge). The 300 mm setback ensures the user's foot detects the tactile warning before the leading foot reaches the drop. Selecting 300 mm as the depth is the documented wrong answer.
common_misconceptions: Selecting depth = 300 mm — 300 mm is the setback distance, not the strip depth
Treating both values as equivalent or interchangeable — they measure completely different things

proposed.explanation: Tactile strip: 600 mm deep (the strip), 300 mm setback (from the hazard). Exam trap: these two numbers are frequently swapped.
